title: Homomorphisms from diagonalizable groups to unipotent groups vanish
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and use affine group schemes and homomorphisms as in [def-sc-group-scheme] and closed subgroup schemes as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Let $M$ be a finitely generated abelian group, written additively. Define $D_k(M)=\operatorname{Spec}k[M]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], where $k[M]$ has basis $e_m$ for $m\in M$, multiplication $e_me_{m'}=e_{m+m'}$, comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, counit $e_m\mapsto1$, and antipode $e_m\mapsto e_{-m}$. The tensor product is over $k$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Let $n\geq1$ and let $\mathcal U_{n,k}$ be the group scheme whose $A$-points are the upper triangular $n\times n$ matrices with entries in $A$ and all diagonal entries $1$, under matrix multiplication, for each commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Let $U\subseteq\mathcal U_{n,k}$ be a closed subgroup scheme. Every group-scheme homomorphism $f:D_k(M)\to U$ is the trivial homomorphism: for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and $d\in D_k(M)(A)$ one has $f_A(d)=1$. No smoothness or connectedness of $D_k(M)$ or $U$ is assumed; in particular torsion in $M$, including torsion of order divisible by $\operatorname{char}k$, is allowed.

source.place: Corollary 14.18(b) and its proof using Proposition 14.16, printed p.284; Theorem 12.8 and Theorem 12.9(c), printed p.233; Theorem 14.5 and Corollary 14.7, printed pp.281--282. This is the direction from multiplicative type to unipotent, not Corollary 14.18(a).

proof.text:
Put $R=k[M]$, with $1=e_0$, and let $g:D_k(M)\to\mathcal U_{n,k}$ be $f$ followed by the subgroup inclusion. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the identity algebra map of $R$ is a universal point $d\in D_k(M)(R)$: every $A$-point is its image under a unique $k$-algebra map $h:R\to A$. Write $g_R(d)=(a_{ij})$, with $a_{ii}=1$ and $a_{ij}=0$ for $i>j$. In $T=R\otimes_kR$, let $d_L,d_R$ be the images of $d$ under the two algebra inclusions of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The group law on $D_k(M)$ makes $d_Ld_R$ the point with algebra map $\Delta:R\to T$. Naturality and the homomorphism property of $g$ therefore give, by matrix multiplication, for $i<j$,
$$\Delta(a_{ij})=a_{ij}\otimes1+1\otimes a_{ij}+\sum_{i<l<j}a_{il}\otimes a_{lj}.$$
This is an identity in $R\otimes_kR$, obtained from actual $T$-points, without a reducedness assumption.

source.place: Theorem 14.5, proof (b) => (c), formula (92), printed p.281; group algebra from Section 12(b), printed pp.230--232. Derivation on the universal point.

proof.text: For $u\in M$ write $c_u:R\to k$ for its coefficient map in the stated basis $e_m$. For $u,v\in M$, the bilinear pairing $(x,y)\mapsto c_u(x)c_v(y)$ induces a linear functional $C_{u,v}:R\otimes_kR\to k$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with $C_{u,v}(e_s\otimes e_t)=\delta_{u,s}\delta_{v,t}$. If $a=\sum_m b_me_m$ satisfies $\Delta(a)=a\otimes1+1\otimes a$, applying $C_{m,m}$ for $m\ne0$ gives $b_m=0$, and applying $C_{0,0}$ gives $b_0=2b_0$, hence $b_0=0$. Thus $a=0$. The last subtraction also holds in characteristic $2$; no division, torsion-freeness of $M$, or independence of geometric points is used.

source.place: Section 12(b), printed pp.230--232, the group-algebra basis and diagonal comultiplication; Section 14(e), printed p.292, formula (95) for primitive elements. Explicit coefficient calculation by Q26, valid in every characteristic.

proof.text: Induct on the height $h=j-i\geq1$ to show $a_{ij}=0$ for every $i<j$. At height $1$ the sum in step 1 is empty, so step 2 applies. If all entries of height less than $h$ vanish and $j-i=h$, then each $a_{il}$ and $a_{lj}$ in that sum has smaller height, so the sum vanishes. Again step 2 gives $a_{ij}=0$. This proves $g_R(d)=I_n$. For $n=1$ there are no off-diagonal entries and this equality holds from the outset.

source.place: Theorem 14.5, formula (92), printed p.281; explicit induction on superdiagonal height by Q26.

proof.text: For any commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and any $x\in D_k(M)(A)$, write $x=h_*(d)$ using its algebra map $h:R\to A$. Naturality gives $g_A(x)=h_*(g_R(d))=h_*(I_n)=I_n$. The inclusion $U(A)\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_{n,k}(A)$ is injective by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] and sends the identity to $I_n$, so $f_A(x)=1$. This proves all the stated clauses. In particular $M=0$, $n=1$, and $M=\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z$ in characteristic $p$ require no changes.

source.place: Corollary 14.18(b), printed p.284; explicit universal-point conclusion, replacing the image argument by the coordinate proof above.
